summary: Memantine is a moderate-affinity, uncompetitive NMDA-receptor antagonist for moderate-to-severe Alzheimer's dementia. It is titrated weekly from 5 mg to a target of 20 mg/day to limit dizziness and confusion. It is renally eliminated; dose is reduced in severe renal impairment, and clearance falls when urine is strongly alkaline. It can be combined with cholinesterase inhibitors.
indications: Treatment of moderate to severe dementia of the Alzheimer's type

dosage.d: Start 5 mg/day; increase by 5 mg weekly to 20 mg/day (10 mg twice daily)
dosage.n: Doses above 5 mg are split twice daily

dosage.d: Start 7 mg/day; increase by 7 mg weekly to target 28 mg once daily
Target 5 mg twice daily (10 mg/day) IR; 14 mg/day ER
dosage.n: Allow >=1 week at each dose step

admin: May be taken with or without food
Titrate at intervals of no less than 1 week between dose increases
Extended-release capsules may be opened and sprinkled on applesauce; swallow without chewing

moa: Memantine is a moderate-affinity, uncompetitive (open-channel) NMDA-receptor antagonist that blocks the sustained, pathological glutamate-driven calcium influx thought to contribute to neuronal dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease, while sparing the brief physiologic activation needed for learning and memory.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to memantine or excipients
relative: Conditions that raise urine pH (renal tubular acidosis, severe UTI with Proteus) - reduced clearance
Recent MI, uncontrolled hypertension or heart failure (caution)

preg: Limited human data. Use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: It is not known whether memantine is excreted in human milk; breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment.
renal: Memantine is mainly renally eliminated. No adjustment for mild-to-moderate impairment; in severe impairment (CrCl 5-29 mL/min) reduce the target dose (10 mg/day IR or 14 mg/day ER).
hepatic: No dose adjustment in mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment; use with caution in severe hepatic impairment (not studied).

moderate: Other NMDA antagonists (amantadine, ketamine, dextromethorphan) - avoid combined use; additive CNS effects
Drugs/conditions that alkalinise urine (carbonic anhydrase inhibitors, sodium bicarbonate) - reduce renal clearance and raise memantine levels
minor: Renally cleared cationic drugs (cimetidine, ranitidine, hydrochlorothiazide, quinidine) - possible altered levels of either drug
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol; may add to CNS adverse effects.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory interference; renal function affects clearance.

monitoring: Cognitive and functional response to therapy
Renal function (especially in elderly and renal impairment)
Conditions that raise urine pH (which reduce clearance)
counsel: The dose is increased slowly over weeks to reduce side effects - follow the titration schedule
May be taken with or without food
If you stop the medicine for several days, do not restart at the full dose - contact your doctor
Report new confusion, dizziness, fainting or seizures
It can be used alongside Alzheimer's medicines such as donepezil
pk: Symptomatic benefit develops over weeks of titration
pearls: Titrate weekly by 5 mg (IR) to limit dizziness and confusion
Renally eliminated - reduce dose in severe renal impairment (CrCl 5-29)
Strongly alkaline urine reduces clearance and can raise levels
Can be combined with cholinesterase inhibitors (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine)
Restart with re-titration after an interruption of several days
missed: If you miss a single dose, do not double up - skip it and take the next dose at the usual time. If several doses are missed, contact your doctor; treatment may need to be restarted with gradual re-titration.
overdose: Reported overdoses caused restlessness, psychosis, visual hallucinations, somnolence, stupor, unsteadiness, loss of consciousness and (rarely) ECG changes. Management is symptomatic and supportive; elimination can be enhanced by acidifying the urine. There is no specific antidote.
